standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes what it means for (H_n) and (H/I^n H) to be isomorphic, which is the primary conclusion.

core_obligations: Rewrite H_n as beta^{-1}(I^n M)/(Im(alpha) + I^n L) and use the inclusions of the two terms to produce the canonical maps H -> H_n and H_n -> H_{n-1} (proof lines 28906-28913).

Apply Artin-Rees twice to choose constants c_1 and c_2 with beta^{-1}(I^n M) contained in Ker(beta) + I^{n-c_1} L for n >= c_1 and Ker(beta) cap I^n L contained in I^{n-c_2} Ker(beta) for n >= c_2, and set c = c_1 + c_2 (proof lines 28916-28920).
Define psi_n : H_n -> H/I^{n-c}H by choosing y in beta^{-1}(I^n M) over x, splitting y = z + w with z in Ker(beta) and w in I^{n-c_1} L, and sending x to the class of z (proof lines 28923-28926).

Prove psi_n is well defined: for a second choice y' = z' + w' one has y' - y = alpha(v) + u with u in I^n L, so u + w - w' lies in Ker(beta) cap I^{n-c_1} L and hence in I^{n-c} Ker(beta) (proof lines 28927-28941).
Verify that the two displayed compositions are the canonical maps, using y - z = w in I^{n-c} L for the second one (proof lines 28944-28957).

Deduce parts (1) to (4) from the existence of these maps, identifying morphisms of pro-objects and using that isomorphic pro-objects have isomorphic limits, and factoring H_{n+c} -> H_n through H/I^n H (proof lines 28960-28968).
Prove part (5) by writing x in I^c H_n as a sum f_i x_i and computing psi_n with the summed choices (proof lines 28971-28978).
Prove part (6) by exhibiting the two annihilation bounds, I^{c_2} killing the class of y in H/I^n H and I^{c_1} carrying the class of fy into the image of H (proof lines 28981-28990).
difficulty_reason: This is a six-part structure theorem. Starting from a complex K -> L -> M of finite modules over a Noetherian ring A with H = Ker(beta)/Im(alpha), and the complexes induced modulo I^n with homology H_n, the lemma produces canonical maps H -> H_n and H_n -> H_{n-1} and then asserts that the pro-systems (H_n) and (H/I^n H) are isomorphic, that their limits agree, that (H_n) is Mittag-Leffler, and three further exactness statements (source lines 28866-28903). The proof must first rewrite H_n as beta^{-1}(I^n M)/(Im(alpha) + I^n L) and build the comparison maps from the inclusions beta^{-1}(I^n M) in beta^{-1}(I^{n-1} M) and Im(alpha) + I^n L in Im(alpha) + I^{n-1} L (proof lines 28906-28913). The genuinely non-routine part is then the construction of the map psi_n : H_n -> H/I^{n-c}H, which depends on two Artin-Rees constants c_1 and c_2 chosen so that beta^{-1}(I^n M) is contained in Ker(beta) + I^{n-c_1} L and Ker(beta) cap I^n L is contained in I^{n-c_2} Ker(beta) (proof lines 28916-28920), together with a well-definedness argument that tracks a second set of choices through those two containments (proof lines 28927-28941). Parts (1) to (6) are then derived, with (5) proved by summing over generators of I^c H_n (proof lines 28971-28978) and (6) by splitting into the two annihilation bounds, one from each Artin-Rees constant, which is why the single exponent c = c_1 + c_2 is what makes the statement true (proof lines 28981-28990).
